title: Long-Distance Rides for Seniors: Getting to Thanksgiving When Family Is an Hour Away
summary: Learn how to arrange long-distance rides for seniors with GoGoGrandparent. Get tips for booking ahead, planning holiday travel, and making trips comfortable.
body_markdown:
If your parent no longer drives, they can still get to your Thanksgiving table an hour or two away. GoGoGrandparent arranges long-distance rides for seniors by phone: a ride can typically go up to 100 miles, depending on driver availability, and an operator at1 (855) 464-6872 can give you a quote and book it in advance. No smartphone, no app, and you don't have to spend the morning of the holiday on the highway twice.


Here is how a long ride works, what you book ahead, and how you make a two-hour trip comfortable for someone who is 80. None of it needs a smartphone.


## **How far can a GoGo ride go?**


Typically up to 100 miles, depending on driver availability. That covers most "the kids live across the state line" trips: the suburb to the city, one county to the next, the coast to the capital. Rides between cities are fine within that range. A trip longer than 100 miles can't be booked the usual way, so if your table is farther than that, call and ask what's possible before you plan around it.


GoGo arranges the ride through Uber or Lyft and matches your parent with a highly rated driver. The GoGo Guardians team is able to monitor the trip. The[rides for seniors](https://www.gogograndparent.com/services/rides-for-seniors) page shows how a booking works, step by step.


## **When should the Thanksgiving ride be booked?**


The week before. Thanksgiving is Thursday, November 26 this year, and[AAA](https://newsroom.aaa.com/2025/11/aaa-thanksgiving-travel-forecast-2025/) expected 73 million Americans to travel by car for the holiday last year. Holiday weeks are busy for drivers too, so call ahead with both addresses and the time your parent needs to arrive, and ask the operator to check driver availability for the trip there and the trip back. Our guide to[scheduling rides in advance](https://www.gogograndparent.com/blog/how-to-schedule-rides-to-upcoming-medical-appointments) walks through the call.


Booking ahead gives the operator time to review both routes with you, explain what to expect for each pickup, and quote the exact ride before you plan the day around it. Three things to tell the operator when you book:


- **The time to arrive, not the time to leave.** Say "dinner is at two," and the operator works the pickup time back from there, with room for holiday traffic.
- **What the driver should know.** A walker, a cane, a service dog, or a slow walk to the car. It goes on the booking.
- **Who is paying.** Once you have been added to your parent's account as someone who can make requests, you can book and pay for the ride from another state.[How GoGoGrandparent works](https://www.gogograndparent.com/blog/how-gogograndparent-works-for-seniors) explains the account in plain words.


## **What makes a long ride comfortable for an older passenger?**


A 20-minute ride needs nothing. A 90-minute ride needs a little planning, and most of it is yours to do before the car arrives.


- **A bathroom stop before pickup, and water in a bottle with a lid.** Long rides and full cups don't mix.
- **A sweater and a small pillow.** Car temperature is the driver's choice, and a pillow behind the lower back makes a long seat belt stretch easier.
- **The host's phone number on a card** in a pocket, in case their phone dies or they need the number handy.
- **The pie in a box on the floor,** not on a lap. Anything that spills should spill on a mat.


## **How does the ride home work after a long dinner?**


Family dinners run long, and nobody should have to leave before the pie because a driver is waiting. The ride home is its own booking: when the evening winds down, you or your parent call1 (855) 464-6872 and ask for the ride, or you schedule a separate pickup in the afternoon once a time looks right. Ask the operator to review the return with you when you book the first leg, so both routes are planned together. If your parent is staying the night, better still: book the ride home for the next morning.


## **Three calls, one holiday**


The ride there, which you book the week before, and the ride back, booked when the pie is done. In between, GoGo makes the call: your parent hears the driver's name and that the car has pulled up, by call or text, whichever they chose. If you're listed as a family contact, GoGo can text you the driver's name and license plate too. GoGoGrandparent has arranged rides for older adults since 2016, and the long ones to family are the ones people call about afterward. One number for all of it:1 (855) 464-6872 .


## **FAQ**


### **How far will GoGoGrandparent take a senior?**


Typically up to 100 miles, depending on driver availability. Call for a quote on your exact trip before you plan the day around it.


### **Can I book my parent's Thanksgiving ride from another state?**


Yes. Once you have been added to the account as someone who can make requests, you can arrange and pay for the ride by phone, and GoGo can text you the driver's name and license plate when the trip starts.


### **What does a long ride cost?**


The Uber or Lyft fare for the distance plus a small concierge fee. Call1 (855) 464-6872 with both addresses for a quote on your exact trip.


### **Does the driver wait and bring my parent back?**


No. The ride home is a second booking, made when your parent is ready to leave or scheduled for a set time. That way nobody has to cut the evening short.
